plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. My value is $31, so bidding $31 ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than the second-highest bid, and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. There's no strategic advantage to shading my bid up or down in this format.

This is a second-price auction, where the winner pays the second-highest bid rather than their own bid. In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value ($17). Bidding higher risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me if I'm the second-highest bidder's price. Bidding lower risks losing an auction I could have profitably won. Since my payment depends on others' bids, not my own, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $7, I will bid exactly $7 to maximize expected profit.
